description: Danna Arrieta-Ventura reflects on her family’s connections to the September 11 attacks and their aftermath. She recounts that her mother, an immigrant from Huánuco, Peru, was studying in high school in New York in 2001 and had limited communication with relatives in Peru. Her great-aunt was in Lima when the attacks occurred, listening to the radio and fearing for Danna’s mother while they were unable to communicate. Danna also shares a story from middle school about her former science teacher’s friend, who worked near the World Trade Center and was surrounded and hidden by coworkers and friends while walking in New York in the weeks afterward. She describes the attacks’ cultural impact and fear as extending beyond the United States, and emphasizes the importance of remembering those effects internationally. Her account centers on family and community memories rather than a claim of personal presence at an attack site.
